text:
Mira: Quick sync — I'm drafting a follow-up to the precision profiles RFC. Idea: expose a single PrecisionLifecycle API that handles profile registration, versioning, canary rollout, and runtime hints. Proposal attached. Want feedback on interface boundaries and backward compatibility.

Sam: +1 to consolidation. Concern: runtime path needs an extremely small fast path (no allocation). API must allow offline compile-time fingerprints to avoid a runtime lookup on the hot path.

Ben: From product — customers will ask for per-customer overrides. How does that map to the API? namespace + overrides?

Tara: I think namespace + explicit priority ordering (customer > service > global). Also need read-only pinned versions for Dedicated/Private customers (can't auto-update).

Jae: ops concern — rollout metadata must include fail-open policy (fallback model or fallback precision) and telemetry hooks (sampled payloads + quality tokens). Also need an atomic bundle publish for safe rollbacks.

Mira: Sketch of the minimal API (pseudo):
```json
{
  "register_profile": {
    "name": "fp8-default",
    "shapes": ["seq256", "seq1024"],
    "quality_budget": "0.002"
  },
  "publish_version": {
    "profile": "fp8-default",
    "version": "v2",
    "canary_pct": "1",
    "fallback": "int8-compat"
  }
}
```
The runtime handshake should be `resolve(profile_id, customer_id) -> fingerprint, allowed_bitpaths, fallback_id`. Fingerprint must be stable across control-plane publishes for hashability.

Sam: runtime impl notes: `resolve` must be cacheable by fingerprint; return must be a tiny struct (id, bitmask, fallback_id). Avoid per-request heap allocs or large JSON parsing.

Ben: Product asks for reason codes in responses so we can surface why a request got downgraded (e.g. `rejected_by_latency_budget`, `rejected_by_quality_guardrail`, `accepted_by_shadow_evidence`). Helpful for customer transparency.

Tara: Also propose a "quality escrow" concept — when we accept downgraded precision we mint a token to track shadow evals against ground truth. That token gets backfilled into observability pipelines.

Mira: Ops can implement shadow sampling + attach `quality_token` to logs. We should standardize sampling rate metadata in the profile.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: profile-v2 -> canary=1% at 2026-04-01T03:00Z :rocket: 

Jae: One more boundary question — should profile resolution live entirely in the control plane or partially in the runtime? My take: control plane resolves and publishes compact fingerprints; runtime only fetches fingerprint + applies tiny local rules (latency budget checks). Keeps runtime code small.

Sam: Agree. Also add a renegotiation hook for long-lived streams (chat). After N tokens or when customer override changes, runtime should re-resolve (non-blocking).

Ben: Policy/legal note — for Private deployments we must support an offline bundle format (signed) so customers can import profiles without control-plane access.

Tara: Migration plan proposal: 1) Introduce `x-precision-profile-id` request header (opt-in). 2) Start publishing fingerprints and signed bundles. 3) Open canary path for control-plane clients. 4) Deprecate per-model boolean flags after 2 quarters.

Mira: Action items: I'll draft the API doc + migration checklist and push a draft PR. Sam/Jae/Tara/Ben please review before EOD Fri. Thanks :v:

Sam: I'll validate the low-allocation shape and post a microbenchmark.

Jae: I'll work on the atomic bundle format and signing scheme.

Ben: I'll update customer-facing FAQ draft for override behavior.

Tara: Adding a checklist item to ensure we have shadow-eval gating and alerting for degradation.

Mira: OK — putting this on the calendar for a quick sync tomorrow 11am if folks want to walk it through.
